title: Natural comparison between raw derived Hom and restricted cohomology
statement: Let $S$ be any scheme [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions], $p\in\mathbb N$ and $U\to S$ any etale scheme. There exists a family of additive isomorphisms $e_{h,F}:A(h,F,U,p)\simeq R(h,F,U,p)$ for every $h:Y\to S$ and every abelian etale sheaf $F$, where $A$ is the raw derived-Hom group of [lem-sbc-abelian-higher-direct-image-natural-comparison] and $R$ is [def-sbc-raw-affine-restricted-cohomology]. For every triangle $a:Y'\to Y$, $h'=ah$ and coefficient map $\phi:a^{-1}F\to F'$, the canonical restricted-cohomology map carries $e_{h,F}(t)$ to $e_{h',F'}$ of the explicit raw pullback of $t$, for every raw class $t$. No affine, qcqs, directed-system or limit hypothesis is assumed.

proof.text: Use the explicitly constructed evaluation morphism. Its invertibility theorem supplies IsIso at every h and F; form asIso without choosing arbitrary data.
The hom of asIso is definitionally the evaluation morphism. Its pullback compatibility theorem therefore gives the required equation pointwise.
